## The Joint Corp. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results


[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_62330c135a82807ad0371ec57c44f5c3/thejoint/news/2026-11-05_The_Joint_Corp_Reports_Third_Quarter_2026_324.pdf) November 05, 2026

[PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_62330c135a82807ad0371ec57c44f5c3/thejoint/db/373/3153/presentation/JYNT_Q3_2026_Results_Deck_FINAL_11-5-26.pdf)


[Presentation](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_62330c135a82807ad0371ec57c44f5c3/thejoint/db/373/3153/presentation/JYNT_Q3_2026_Results_Deck_FINAL_11-5-26.pdf)


*- Revenue Increases to $13.6 Million -*


*- Net Income from Continuing Operations Increases by $1.2 Million to $1.5 Million and Adjusted EBITDA From Continuing Operations Increases by $0.9 Million to $2.3 Million -*


*-* *Continued Execution on Capital Allocation Priorities with Regional Developer Territory Buybacks and $3.8 Million in Stock Repurchases -*


*- Board of Directors Authorizes an Additional $5.0 Million for Stock Repurchases -*


SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Nov. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The Joint Corp. (NASDAQ: JYNT), the nation's largest franchisor of chiropractic care through *The Joint Chiropractic* ® network, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. The following figures represent continuing operations unless otherwise stated. The Company also updated its full year 2026 guidance (see details below).


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights**


- Revenues grew to $13.6 million, up 1% compared to the third quarter of 2025.
- System-wide sales1 were $123.3 million, a 3.1% decrease compared to the third quarter of 2025.
- Reported comp sales2 of (1.9)%, compared to (2.8)% in the second quarter of 2026.
- Net loss from consolidated operations was $117,000, compared to net income from consolidated operations of $855,000 in the third quarter of 2025. Net income from continuing operations was $1.5 million, compared to net income from continuing operations of $290,000 in the third quarter of 2025.
- Adjusted EBITDA (a non-GAAP metric) from consolidated operations was $3.3 million, in line with $3.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations was $2.3 million, compared to $1.4 million in the third quarter of 2025.
- Cash flow used in operating activities was $128,000, compared to cash provided by operating activities of $1.8 million in the third quarter of 2025, and free cash flow (a non-GAAP metric) was $(509,000), compared to $1.5 million in the third quarter of 2025.
- Repurchased 461,000 shares for total consideration of approximately $3.8 million at an average of $8.30 per share during the third quarter.


**Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Operating Highlights**


- On October 1, 2026, the Company reacquired the regional developer (“RD”) rights for Texas, a region consisting of 141 franchised clinics, for total cash consideration of $8.0 million due at closing and up to $2.0 million in potential additional consideration payments if certain gross sales metrics are met or exceeded in the Texas region during the two annual periods following the closing.


- Year to date in 2026, the Company has reacquired the RD rights to five territories, including Texas, consisting of 189 franchised clinics. These efforts will lead to the realization of approximately $3.0 million in reduced RD royalties on an annualized basis, with approximately one-third of this benefit being offset by internal costs to manage these territories.


- Total clinic count was 930 at September 30, 2026.


- Opened four clinics, closed 15 clinics, and refranchised 26 clinics during the quarter, for a total of 915 franchised clinics and 15 company-owned or managed clinics at September 30, 2026.


1 System-wide sales include revenues at all clinics, whether operated or managed by the Company or by franchisees. While franchised sales are not recorded as revenues by the Company, management believes the information is important in understanding the Company’s financial performance because these revenues are the basis on which the Company calculates and records royalty fees and are indicative of the financial health of the franchisee base.


2 Comp sales include the revenues from both company-owned or managed clinics and franchised clinics that in each case have been open at least 13 full months and exclude any clinics that have closed.


“Our third quarter results reflect growth in our active membership count as well as in the lifetime value per active member,” said President and Chief Executive Officer of The Joint Corp., Sanjiv Razdan. “By leaning into our value proposition, especially with our newer flexible membership options, we are driving more members to stay with us longer. Primarily reflecting the ongoing macroeconomic challenges, growth in these metrics is partially offset by lower average patient spend per month and fewer new patients, which is continuing to impact our comps. We believe our ability to grow our active membership count and our stronger new clinic performance is strengthening our foundation for future growth.


“Our success with our clinic refranchising efforts has positioned The Joint as a pure-play franchisor model, which, combined with RD territory buybacks already completed this year, is helping to drive margin improvement, profitability and cash flow. With our strong balance sheet and improving cash generation from continuing operations, we have the financial flexibility to continue to execute simultaneously on our growth strategies, RD territory buybacks and continued stock repurchase capital allocation priorities. Our additional $5 million stock repurchase authorization reflects our confidence that our asset-light franchise model and initiatives to reignite growth will help create long-term value for our stockholders.”


**Continued Execution on Stock Repurchase Program**


The Company’s initiative to refranchise previously company-owned or managed clinics to drive higher cash flows derived from an asset-light franchise model began in 2023, opening a pathway for the Company to begin executing on its first stock repurchase program. Since June 3, 2025, the Company has repurchased 1,975,352 shares for total consideration of $17 million.


During the third quarter of 2026, the Company repurchased approximately 461,000 shares for total consideration of approximately $3.8 million, at an average price of $8.30 per share. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had exhausted the full $12 million of the latest authorization for repurchasing shares.


On November 3, 2026, the Company’s Board of Directors authorized an additional $5 million for stock repurchases. Repurchases under this program may be made from time to time in open market transactions, privately negotiated transactions, or by other means in accordance with applicable securities laws and are subject to market conditions and other factors. The timing, frequency and amount of any repurchases will be determined by the Company’s management and Board of Directors. The stock repurchase program does not obligate the Company to acquire any particular amount of common stock.


**Update on Refranchising Efforts**


The Company has substantially completed the refranchising initiative under its Joint 2.0 strategy through previously announced clinic sale bundles:


- **Southern California Bundle:** Forty of the 45 clinics have been refranchised to date.
- **Northern California Bundle:** All four of these clinics have been refranchised to date.
- **Southeast Bundle:** Ten of the 20 clinics have been refranchised to date.


As a result of these refranchising efforts, The Company now operates as a capital-light, pure-play franchisor, allowing management to concentrate on driving growth through franchise system support, new patient acquisition, and long-term network development.


**Financial Results for Third Quarter Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to September 30, 2025**


Revenue totaled $13.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $13.4 million in the third quarter of 2025, reflecting the Company's continued transition to a pure-play franchisor revenue model. Cost of revenues was $2.4 million, down 10% compared to the prior-year period, primarily due to lower RD royalty costs as the Company continues to reacquire RD territories.


Selling and marketing expenses were $2.7 million, a decrease of 4% compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to lower system-wide sales. Depreciation and amortization expenses were $262,000. General and administrative expenses decreased 6% to $6.9 million compared to $7.3 million in the third quarter of 2025, underscoring ongoing operating discipline within the leaner post-refranchising structure.


Consolidated net loss was $117,000, compared to a consolidated net income of $855,000 in the prior-year period. Net income from continuing operations was $1.5 million, compared to $290,000 in the third quarter of 2025. Consolidated EPS was $(0.01) per share, compared to $0.06 per diluted share in the third quarter of 2025.


Adjusted EBITDA from consolidated operations was $3.3 million, in line with $3.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations was $2.3 million, compared to $1.4 million in the prior-year period.


**Balance Sheet**


Unrestricted cash was $18.3 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $22.2 million at June 30, 2026. The Company maintains a currently undrawn line of credit with JPMorgan Chase Bank, which provides immediate access to $20 million through August 2029.


**Financial Results for Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to September 30, 2025**


Revenue was $43.6 million in the first nine months of 2026, up 10% compared to $39.7 million in the same period in 2025. Consolidated net income was $1.8 million, compared to $1.9 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Net income from continuing operations was $2.3 million, compared to a net loss from continuing operations of $1.2 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Consolidated EPS was $0.13 per diluted share, compared to $0.12 per diluted share in the prior-year period.


Adjusted EBITDA from consolidated operations increased to $9.9 million and Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations increased to $5.9 million, compared to Adjusted EBITDA from consolidated operations of $9.4 million and Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations of $1.5 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025.


**2026 Guidance**


Reflecting continued macroeconomic pressures on consumer spending and the reported financial results for the first nine months of 2026, the Company today updated its 2026 full year financial guidance provided on August 6, 2026, as follows:


- System-wide sales are now expected to be between $508 million and $512 million as compared to the prior range of $519 million to $552 million.
- System-wide comp sales for clinics open 13 months or more are now expected to be in the range of (3.5)% to (2.5)% as compared to the prior range of (3)% to 3%.
- Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is unchanged and is expected to be in the range of $12.5 million to $13.5 million.


The Company continues to work with franchise owners to optimize the performance of the existing franchised clinic base. This will include closing underperforming clinics this year, which will result in the overall clinic count at 2026 year-end being approximately 50 clinics lower than 2025 year-end.

**About The Joint Corp. (NASDAQ: JYNT)**


The Joint Corp. (NASDAQ: JYNT) revolutionized access to chiropractic care when it introduced its retail healthcare business model in 2010. Today, it is the nation’s largest operator, manager and franchisor of chiropractic clinics through The Joint Chiropractic network. The Company is making quality care convenient and affordable, while eliminating the need for insurance, for millions of patients seeking pain relief and ongoing wellness. Headquartered in Scottsdale and with over 925 locations nationwide and more than 14 million patient visits annually, The Joint Chiropractic is a key leader in the chiropractic industry. The brand is consistently named to *Franchise Times’* annual “Top 400” and “Fast & Serious” list of smartest growing brands. *Entrepreneur* named The Joint “No. 1 in Chiropractic Services,” and it is regularly ranked on the publication’s “Franchise 500®,” “Fastest-Growing Franchises,” and “Best of the Best” lists, as well as its “Top Franchise for Veterans” and “Top Brands for Multi-Unit Owners” rankings. *SUCCESS®* named the Company one of the “Top 50 Franchises”. The Joint Chiropractic is an innovative force where healthcare meets retail. **Business Structure**


The Joint Corp. is a franchisor of clinics and an operator of clinics in certain states. In Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, District of Columbia, Florida, Illinois, Kansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Washington, and West Virginia, The Joint Corp. and its franchisees provide management services to affiliated professional chiropractic practices.


**Commonly Discussed Performance Metrics**


This release includes a presentation of commonly discussed performance metrics. System-wide sales include revenues at all clinics, whether operated by the Company or by franchisees. While franchised sales are not recorded as revenues by the Company, management believes the information is important in understanding the Company’s financial performance because these sales are the basis on which the Company calculates and records royalty fees and are indicative of the financial health of the franchisee base. Comp sales include the revenues from both company-owned or managed clinics and franchised clinics that in each case have been open at least 13 full months and exclude any clinics that have closed.


**Non-GAAP Financial Information**


This release also includes a presentation of non-GAAP financial measures. EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are presented because they are important measures used by management to assess financial performance, as management believes they provide a more transparent view of the Company’s underlying operating performance and operating trends. Free cash flow is presented as a supplemental measure of liquidity. Reconciliation of historical net income/(loss) to EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA and reconciliation of operating activities cash flows to free cash flow is presented in the tables below. The Company defines EBITDA as net income/(loss) before net interest, tax expense, depreciation, and amortization expenses. The Company defines Adjusted EBITDA as EBITDA before acquisition-related expenses (which includes contract termination costs associated with reacquired RD rights), net (gain)/loss on disposition or impairment, stock-based compensation expenses, costs related to restatement filings, restructuring costs, and litigation expenses (consisting of legal and related fees for specific proceedings that arise outside of the ordinary course of our business). The Company defines free cash flow as net cash provided by (used in) operating activities less capital expenditures. EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow do not represent and should not be considered alternatives to net income or cash flows from operations, as determined by accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (“GAAP”). While EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are used as measures of financial performance and free cash flow is used as a measure of liquidity, they are not necessarily comparable to other similarly titled captions of other companies due to potential inconsistencies in the methods of calculation. EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow should be reviewed in conjunction with the Company’s financial statements filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”). Please refer to the reconciliations of non-GAAP financial measures to their GAAP equivalents located at the end of this release. This release includes forward-looking guidance for certain non-GAAP financial measures, including Adjusted EBITDA. These measures will differ from net income (loss), determined in accordance with GAAP, in ways similar to those described in the reconciliations at the end of this release. We are not able to provide, without unreasonable effort, guidance for net income (loss), determined in accordance with GAAP, or a reconciliation of guidance for Adjusted EBITDA to the most directly comparable GAAP measure because the Company is not able to predict with reasonable certainty the amount or nature of all items that will be included in net income (loss).
